Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medicore's security team has a couple of follow-ups on retention and deletion behavior we need to lock into the DPA annex before procurement can sign off. Our two asks are: 1) an explicit staggered purge timetable across primary/replica/backups (we need to know max retention in each tier), and 2) a simple escrow/rollback mechanism if we need a short-term emergency restore (e.g., legal hold or incident response).

Specifically they want:
- Maximum bucket-level backup TTL for hot-replay snapshots
- Confirmation on whether subprocessor copies (third-party backups) will be subject to the same purge trigger
- A documented emergency restore process and SLA (how many days to provide a restore and what triggers authorization)

Can you send a short proposed annex (plain language + timeline)? Also please include the current subprocessor list and whether any of them are outside the EU/US (cross-border). We can then have LegalOps review.

Thanks,

Subject: DPA annex language proposal (staggered purge + rollback)

Hi Alice —

Attached is proposed plain-language text that we suggest including as Annex B (Backup & Deletion Controls). Key points in this draft:

1) Tiered purge timetable (examples):
   - Hot snapshots / KV caches: purge after 3 days; emergency rollback available for up to 7 days.
   - Replica buffers / short-term backups: purge after 30 days; emergency rollback available for up to 30 days subject to authorization.
   - Cold archives / long-term backup copies: purge after 90 days; restore possible within 90 days but subject to subprocessor data retrieval SLA.

2) Subprocessor parity: We commit to use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure subprocessors observe the same purge triggers. Where subprocessors have longer retention due to operational constraints we will notify Customer and provide an escrow plan.

3) Emergency restore & rollback mechanism:
   - Customer may request a one-time emergency restore on written notice to Security@redwood.ai.
   - We will confirm feasibility within 48 hours and provide an estimated restore window.
   - For restores older than 30 days, the restore may require data retrieval from cold storage and incur retrieval fees; timing will be shared in the feasibility response.

4) Irrevocable destruction certification: upon purge completion Redwood will provide a certificate of destruction for primary systems; for subprocessor-held copies we will provide attestation that we have requested deletion and will track completion.

Karthik and Marissa included minor ops details in the annex about snapshot tagging and labels used to trigger cascaded purges. If Medicore is comfortable with these levels I suggest LegalOps take this copy and submit redlines.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference

Kimberly — thanks for the thorough draft. A few clarifying redline requests from our side:  

- We need a defined authorization cadence for emergency restores (who signs off internally at Medicore) and a one-hour SLA to acknowledge receipt of the request (we're OK with 48 hours for feasibility if acknowledgement is faster).
- For subprocessor deletions, Medicore requires a 15-day escrow window where Redwood will retain an encrypted, access-controlled retrieval token that Medicore can use only under joint authorization for legal holds. This is a non-negotiable technical safeguard for our auditors.
- Can you commit to providing log-level metadata (hash + timestamp) as part of the destruction attestation? Full content is not required, just stream-level checksums and timestamps for audit.

We will prepare a short redline and upload via DocuSign. Also please confirm whether any of your subprocessors are in APAC — our policy requires advance notice for cross-border backups.

Regards,
Medicore LegalOps
